key_insight: Mixing nanoscale Laponite with microscale Bentonite reduces drying damage, with most intermediate compositions on glass outperforming a simple average of the pure-clay endpoints.
engineering_relevance: Clay composition offers a practical lever for improving drying-damage resistance in coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing.
method: Compare drying damage across clay compositions on hydrophobic polypropylene and hydrophilic glass.
Measure two-step yielding in gelled suspensions and derive cohesive energies from each step.
Use an energy-balance-derived cohesion–adhesion index to interpret peeling versus cracking.
evidence_signal: Replicate experiments showed essentially intact Laponite films, extensive Bentonite fracture and two-step yielding in every composition.
watch_item: Rheology–cracking correlations must specify the yielding step used, because derived cohesive energies differ by orders of magnitude.
paper_title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
